# The Problem {.center}

## The talk

::: {.incident}
::: {.tag}
Conference · Session 4B · Thursday 2:15 PM
:::

**Agents That Read So You Don't: Automating Literature Review with LLMs**

Chen, Okafor & Ruiz
:::

::: {.fragment .why style="text-align:center"}
That's **our** project.
:::

::: {.fragment .why style="text-align:center"}
It was posted to arXiv **three weeks ago**.
:::

::: {.notes}
- Tell it as a story. Mateo's lab has worked on this for a year. They sit down at a conference talk and watch someone else present it.
- The PI leans over: "How did we miss this?"
- Pause on the second line. It was public. Anyone could have seen it.
:::

- It's tedious, so it's easy to rush. The paper was in his results; he scrolled past.
- This isn't a Mateo problem. It's a "humans are bad at tedious, repeated work" problem.
:::

- OPEN (from the Colab test): the no-tools notebook agent didn't say "I can't". It made up 3 plausible papers with fake arXiv IDs. If we keep the notebook's version, this bubble could show the confident fake digest instead. That's scarier, and it's what students will see in section 3.

:::

## Plug it in {auto-animate=true .compact}

::: {.tag}
Colab · notebook 1-7
:::

```{.python code-line-numbers="7-10"}
from langchain.mcp import MCPAdapter

config = {"mcpServers": {
    "arxiv": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["arxiv-mcp-server"]},
}}

async with MCPAdapter(config) as adapter:
    tools = await adapter.list_tools()

print(len(tools), "tools")
```

::: {.why}
Ask the server what it has. **Print the tools before any LLM runs.**
:::

## Plug it in {auto-animate=true .compact}

::: {.tag}
Colab · notebook 1-7
:::

```{.python code-line-numbers="12-20"}
from langchain.mcp import MCPAdapter

config = {"mcpServers": {
    "arxiv": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["arxiv-mcp-server"]},
}}

async with MCPAdapter(config) as adapter:
    tools = await adapter.list_tools()

print(len(tools), "tools")

SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    f"Today is {date.today()}. You are the research assistant for Mateo's lab. "
    "Use your tools; don't guess about papers."
)

agent = create_agent(MODEL, tools, system_prompt=SYSTEM_PROMPT)
result = await agent.ainvoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": FRIDAY}]})

print(result["messages"][-1].text)
```

::: {.why}
Same request, same model. Now it has tools.
:::

::: {.notes}
- `date.today()` is there because the model assumed it was 2024 when it picked search dates.
- `MODEL` and `FRIDAY` come from the "I can't" cell earlier in the notebook.
:::

::: {.notes}
- Start on the left: recap 1.6. Someone else started the server; we only knew its URL.
- (1) Today there's no second machine.
- (2) `uvx` downloads the package and starts it **as a child of your agent**. No URL, no port.
- (3) They talk through the process's own input and output: stdin and stdout.
- (4) Who talks to arxiv.org? The **server**, not the agent. The processing happens on your machine. (Quiz item d asks this.)
- (5) LangChain opens one session per tool call. For stdio, the server starts for the call and exits when it returns. That's why the tools still work after the `async with` block.
:::

### stdio: Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man

::: {.incremental}
- **Local.** On your machine
- **Swoops in** when your agent calls, gone after
- **Everyone gets their own** (the Spider-Verse)
- `uvx ...` · `npx ...`
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%" .fragment}
```{=html}

    <circle r="62" fill="none" stroke="#79c0ff" stroke-width="10" stroke-dasharray="18 9"/>
    <circle r="40" fill="#161b22" stroke="#79c0ff" stroke-width="3"/>

    <circle r="12" fill="#79c0ff"/>
  </g>
</svg>
```

### HTTP: Stark Industries

- **Remote.** Someone else's machine
- **Always on**, before you connect
- **Serves many clients** at once
- `https://docs.langchain.com/mcp`
:::
::::

# One Agent, Two Servers {.center}

## One more entry {auto-animate=true .compact}

```{.python}
config = {"mcpServers": {
    "arxiv": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["arxiv-mcp-server"]},
}}
```

## One more entry {auto-animate=true .compact}

```{.python code-line-numbers="1-2,6"}
ARXIV_FOLDER = "/root/.arxiv-mcp-server/papers"   # where the arXiv server saves papers
LAB_FOLDER = "/content/lab_papers"                # where the lab looks

config = {"mcpServers": {
    "arxiv": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["arxiv-mcp-server"]},
    "files": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", LAB_FOLDER, ARXIV_FOLDER]},
}}
```

::: {.why}
The folders at the end of `args` are the **only** folders it can touch.
:::

::: {.notes}
- `npx` is Node's `uvx`. This server is written in TypeScript, and Colab already has Node.
- Two folders: the lab's, and the arXiv server's hidden one, so the agent can move papers across.
:::

## Then ask for the whole Friday {.compact}

```{.python}
FRIDAY = (
    f"Find this week's new arXiv papers on {TOPIC}. Pick the 3 most relevant and download them. "
    f"Move each downloaded paper's .md file from {ARXIV_FOLDER} into {LAB_FOLDER}. "
    f"Then save {LAB_FOLDER}/digest.md with each paper's title, arXiv link, and a 2-sentence summary."
)
```

::: {.why}
Same agent code as before. Only the config and the request changed.
:::

# Pair Quiz {.center}

## Pair quiz (5 min)

::: {.quiz-grid}
::: {.card}
[a.]{.ct}

How do **stdio** and **HTTP** servers differ?
:::
::: {.card}
[b.]{.ct}

What problems does **MCP** solve?
:::
::: {.card}
[c.]{.ct}

What can an MCP server **offer**?
:::
::: {.card}
[d.]{.ct}

Two configs, next slide: which is which, and **where does the work happen**?
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
- Pairs, notes app or paper, no Colab. Put the next slide up too so they can do (d).
- Then walk through the answers one slide at a time. Call on pairs before revealing.
:::

## d. Which is which?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.tag}
Config A
:::

```{.python}
config = {"mcpServers": {
    "fetch": {"command": "uvx",
              "args": ["mcp-server-fetch"]},
}}
```

::: {.answer .fragment data-fragment-index="1"}
**stdio.** Runs on **your machine**, even though it fetches web pages.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.tag}
Config B
:::

```{.python}
config = {"mcpServers": {
    "docs": {"url": "https://docs.langchain.com/mcp"},
}}
```

::: {.answer .fragment data-fragment-index="1"}
**HTTP.** Runs on **LangChain's machine**. You only send requests.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
- The trap: "fetch touches the internet, so it must be HTTP." No. The transport is about how *your agent* talks to the *server*, not what the server does.
- `command` → your agent starts it → your machine. `url` → someone else started it → their machine.
:::

## a. stdio vs HTTP

| | stdio (Spider-Man) | HTTP (Stark) |
|---|---|---|
| Who starts the server | **your agent**, per call | **the owner**, and it stays up |
| Where it runs | your machine | their machine |
| Your config says | `"command"` | `"url"` |
| Clients per server | one | many |
| Today's examples | arXiv, filesystem, fetch | LangChain docs |

::: {.notes}
- Bring the "Where does it run?" diagram back (next slide) if pairs mixed these up.
:::

## b. What problems does MCP solve?

::: {.cards}
::: {.card .fragment style="border-color:#ff7b72"}
[🔧 Tools you don't own]{.ct}

The owner ships and maintains them. They change the code; your agent doesn't break.

*Ludwig, 1.6*
:::

::: {.card .fragment style="border-color:#79c0ff"}
[🔌 One standard]{.ct}

Any agent, any server. Like USB.

*Stark and Spider-Man both plug in the same way*
:::

::: {.card .fragment style="border-color:#7ee787"}
[📦 Someone already built it]{.ct}

Common capabilities ship as servers. You plug them in.

*Mateo, today*
:::
:::

## c. What can a server offer?

::: {.cards}
::: {.card style="border-color:#7ee787"}
[🔧 Tools]{.ct}

Functions the model **calls**.

`search_papers`, `move_file`
:::

::: {.card .fragment style="border-color:#79c0ff"}
[📄 Resources]{.ct}

Data the app can **read**.

*Like a file the server shares*
:::

::: {.card .fragment style="border-color:#d2a8ff"}
[💬 Prompts]{.ct}

Templates the **user** picks.

*A server's best script for a job*
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
- Recap from the 1.6 prep reading.
- LangChain's `MCPAdapter` only loads **tools** today; prompts and resources aren't supported yet. That's why we've only used tools.
:::

# Your Agent {.center}

## Three servers, one agent {.compact}

::: {.tag}
Your Project 1 agent · main.py
:::

```{.python code-line-numbers="1-6|8-11"}
config = {"mcpServers": {
    "docs":  {"url": "https://docs.langchain.com/mcp"},
    "files": {"command": "npx",
              "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", NOTES_FOLDER]},
    # "???": one you pick
}}

async def build_agent():
    async with MCPAdapter(config) as adapter:
        mcp_tools = await adapter.list_tools()
    return create_agent(MODEL, mcp_tools + my_tools)
```

::: {.why}
Your 1.6 `build_agent`, with the URL swapped for a config. Locally you need **uv** and **Node**.
:::

::: {.notes}
- `NOTES_FOLDER` is an absolute path to a folder they choose. Don't give it your home directory.
- stdio servers now run on *their laptop*. Same code; the machine changed.
- Every server counts toward the "most MCP servers connected" leaderboard.
:::
